extracted.intended_audience: K99/R00 applicants and NIH grant reviewers (investigators preparing human subjects, recruitment, and institutional environment sections)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required content for the human subjects, recruitment, inclusion, protection, institutional environment, letters of support, and timeline portions of a K99/R00 NIH application. Focuses on eligibility, recruitment/retention, data protection, IRB/monitoring, partner commitments, and project timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor / Advisor commitment and expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters from mentors/advisors should document mentoring provided, mentor qualifications, and specific commitments to support the candidate (e.g., quarterly meetings, advising on study design, recruitment, retention, and grant-writing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in letters: meeting quarterly in person or by phone; advising on study design and recruitment/retention; providing career development and grant-writing support; stating willingness to consult more often during critical periods. Mentor should be an internationally-recognized expert where relevant and describe relevant prior mentoring and translational experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate research productivity and career-stage appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Application should convey the applicant's research record appropriate for career stage (e.g., number of publications, first-authored papers, manuscripts under review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counts and venues (e.g., 'published 8 articles (4 first-authored) and 4 manuscripts under review') to demonstrate productivity relative to career stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translational and clinical potential, and cultural inclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed project should have translational and clinical potential to improve care and explicitly address cultural inclusivity and disparities (e.g., attention to needs of African American families).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how intervention/training/tool will be culturally inclusive, address disparities in outcomes, incorporate implicit bias awareness, and be translatable into real-world clinical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional environment and available resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe institutional resources that will enable implementation and career development (e.g., offices for faculty development/diversity, centers, CTSC, libraries, software, statistical consultation, IT support, office space, equipment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List concrete resources (e.g., CTSC training/workshops, CRELC resources, in-house IT, software like Stata/SAS/R/NVivo, administrative support, REDCap access) and institutional activities (didactics, seminars, workshops, grand rounds) that support the project and candidate development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to recruitment sites and community partners (letters of support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide letters and descriptions documenting partner organizations' willingness to assist with recruitment, outreach, identification of participants, and adaptation/pilot testing of materials (e.g., CaringKind, VNSNY, clinic sites).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should specify how partners will help (e.g., review patient lists, mail recruitment letters co-signed by PI and medical director, advertise on social media/website/email, help identify and condense training content, assist pilot testing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects determination and clinical trial designation
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether human subjects are involved, whether the project is exempt from federal regulations (and exemption number), and whether it is a clinical trial (and provide ClinicalTrials.gov identifier if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete Clinical Trial Questionnaire items: involvement of participants, prospective assignment to an intervention, whether study is designed to evaluate intervention effect, and whether the effect evaluated is a health-related biomedical or behavioral outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria (participant definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define eligibility for each participant type (e.g., clinicians: nurse or social worker providing home hospice care to patients with dementia; family caregivers: family member providing care to community-dwelling patient with dementia nearing end of life; research/content experts: team member or collaborator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include any race/ethnicity criteria (e.g., family caregivers: African American or white), profession-specific criteria, and other inclusion characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age limits and inclusion/exclusion of children
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify minimum and maximum ages and state whether children are included or excluded (e.g., Min Age: 19 Years, Max Age: 90 Years; individuals under 18 not included).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify exclusion of minors if relevant (e.g., training/education requirements for clinicians).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of women and minorities (demographic targets & reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe plans for inclusion of women and minority participants, expected demographic percentages, and any deliberate sampling by race/ethnicity (e.g., equal numbers of African-American and white caregivers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide expected gender composition for participant pools (e.g., estimate 60-70% female among family caregivers; workforce composition estimates), anticipated racial/ethnic breakdowns (e.g., 65% white, 30% black, 5% other, 15% Hispanic), and attach Inclusion Enrollment Report documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment methods and materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a recruitment plan specifying methods and materials (e.g., review of patient lists, mailed recruitment letters co-signed by PI and medical director, outreach through partner organizations, attending team meetings, recruitment emails).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail site-specific procedures (e.g., VNSNY staff identify hospice patients; study team attends division meetings to explain study), contingency plans (expand to CaringKind and other community organizations if targets unmet), and sources (clinic patient lists, hospice records).

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention strategies and minimizing participant burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe retention approaches for multi-stage studies (e.g., explain overall goals, emphasize importance of contribution, obtain contact info for follow-up, minimize burden by keeping interviews ~40 minutes and offering convenient modalities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For follow-up feedback rounds, generate manageable content for review and a short guiding question list to reduce participant burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size and enrollment targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide numeric enrollment targets by study component and participant type (e.g., Aim 1: 40 family caregivers, 20 clinicians; Aim 2: 10 family caregivers, 5 clinicians; plus research/content experts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State how totals account for overlap across aims (e.g., interview participants who also participate in stakeholder feedback) and include timelines for enrollment and first subject dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study timeline, milestones, and iterative analysis plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Present a quarter-by-quarter timeline across K99 and R00 phases including IRB submissions, data collection, concurrent iterative qualitative analysis (constant comparative technique), development and refinement of training/tool, modified Delphi stakeholder input, feasibility testing, pilot efficacy testing, manuscript preparation, and R00 application preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate when IRB approvals are expected, when interviews/data collection will occur, when stakeholder feedback and feasibility testing will take place, and when manuscripts and subsequent applications will be prepared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of human subjects: data collection procedures and sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe data collection methods (e.g., interviews, baseline assessments, audio-recording with consent), and sources of materials (e.g., electronic medical records used solely for identifying eligible participants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State that audio-files will be transcribed then destroyed; participants may participate without consenting to recording; baseline assessments include demographic data and caregiver-specific measures (religion, discrimination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data confidentiality, identifiers, storage, and access controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe assignment of unique identifiers, storage of linking document on secure WCM server, password protection, locked offices, and that coded data stored on secure server or password-protected REDCap with access limited to credentialed study personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify technical and physical safeguards (single document linking IDs stored in single secure folder accessible only to credentialed personnel on password-protected computers in locked offices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Risks to participants and mitigation/referral procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify potential risks (minimal physical harm; potential emotional distress from interviews; rare discovery of abuse) and provide mitigation and referral procedures (encourage speaking with PCP, provide Eldercare Locator hotline, consult social worker/psychiatrist, refer to appropriate care; report abuse to PCP or practice social worker).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document plans to consult named personnel (e.g., social worker Marlena Palombo, psychiatrist Robert Abrams) and procedures for escalation and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plan and DSMB decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Data and Safety Monitoring Plan document and state whether a Data and Safety Monitoring Board will be appointed (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach the plan (19S1e. Data Safety and Monitoring.pdf) and justify DSMB status (in this study, No).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-site study determination and single IRB plan if applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the study is multi-site using the same protocol at more than one domestic site and, if yes, describe the single IRB plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark applicable choice (Yes/No/N/A) and provide single IRB plan when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Existing Dataset or Resource declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the study uses an existing dataset or resource for enrollment or analysis (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If No, indicate planned domestic enrollment locations and provide comments; if Yes, describe dataset/resource and any limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion Enrollment Reporting (IER) and site details
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Inclusion Enrollment Reports listing enrollment locations (Domestic/Foreign), specific institutions, and planned/actual enrollment counts by race/ethnicity and sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the IER with discrete categories (racial categories, ethnic categories, sex) and cumulative actual counts, and list enrollment location types and comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination plan to stakeholders and participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how findings will be disseminated (e.g., presentations at partner institutions, sharing electronic/mailed copies of presentations and manuscripts with participants who request them).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include plans to present at WCM, VNSNY and CaringKind and to share outputs with participants who indicate interest.
